purpose: Agent vocabulary for camera movements, angles, framing and optical controls
units: metric; seconds; degrees; full-frame-equivalent focal length

catalog.name: Static / Locked-off
catalog.definition: Tripod or virtual camera remains stationary; subject motion supplies action.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Keep camera completely fixed; no pan, tilt, translation or zoom.

catalog.name: Pan left / right
catalog.definition: Camera rotates horizontally from a fixed position.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Pan smoothly right 25 degrees over 4 seconds; pivot around camera location.
catalog.usage: reveal a room or follow passing motion

catalog.name: Tilt up / down
catalog.definition: Camera rotates vertically without changing position.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Tilt upward from wheel assembly to sensor mast over 5 seconds.
catalog.usage: establish height or reveal tall machinery

catalog.name: Dolly in / push-in
catalog.definition: Entire camera translates physically toward subject; perspective changes.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Dolly forward 1.5 m over 5 seconds toward the machine chest plate.

catalog.name: Dolly out / pullback
catalog.definition: Camera translates away from subject; frame and spatial context expand.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Dolly backward 2 m, revealing the full rover and terrain.

catalog.name: Truck / lateral dolly
catalog.definition: Camera travels sideways, approximately perpendicular to viewing direction.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Truck left 2 m while keeping the robot centered.

catalog.name: Pedestal up / down
catalog.definition: Camera moves vertically with orientation held constant.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Pedestal upward 1 m to inspect upper chassis without tilting.

catalog.name: Crane / jib rise
catalog.definition: Camera travels along an arc or vertical sweep on boom, often combining translation and tilt.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Crane up from tire level to a high three-quarter angle in 6 seconds.

catalog.name: Arc / orbit
catalog.definition: Camera travels around subject along an arc while generally facing it.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Orbit clockwise 60 degrees around rover at constant radius.

catalog.name: 360-degree orbit
catalog.definition: Complete circular camera movement around an object.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Orbit one full turn over 12 seconds, fixed radius and fixed subject anchor.
catalog.usage: product turntables; may be too fast for 5-second clips

catalog.name: Tracking / follow
catalog.definition: Camera translates with a moving subject, matching or coordinating speed.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Track alongside moving rover from 3 m away at wheel-center height.

catalog.name: Lead / backward tracking
catalog.definition: Camera moves backward ahead of the advancing subject.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Retreat steadily as robot advances toward lens; maintain 4 m distance.

catalog.name: Reveal / occlusion pass
catalog.definition: Camera crosses an obstruction or foreground element to expose a subject.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Slide right from behind a girder to reveal the suspended drone.

catalog.name: Push-pull / dolly zoom
catalog.definition: Camera dolly and focal-length zoom in opposite directions; subject size remains nearly fixed.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Dolly in while widening focal length to hold subject size and expand background.
catalog.usage: strong perspective shift; difficult to generate accurately

catalog.name: Optical zoom in / out
catalog.definition: Change focal length without moving camera; framing changes with minimal parallax.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Zoom from 35 mm to 70 mm, camera position locked.

catalog.name: Digital zoom / crop
catalog.definition: Simulated magnification by cropping; no new perspective or real detail.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Apply a subtle 1.1x digital crop on an existing frame.

catalog.name: Whip pan
catalog.definition: Very fast pan producing motion blur and often a transition.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Whip pan left in 0.4 seconds to the next assembly.

catalog.name: Handheld
catalog.definition: Small organic translations and rotations associated with a handheld operator.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Subtle stabilized handheld movement; amplitude under 2% frame.

catalog.name: Steadicam / gimbal walk
catalog.definition: Smooth stabilized movement that can travel freely and change direction.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Gimbal walk through workshop aisle at human eye level, smooth horizon.

catalog.name: Drone flyover
catalog.definition: Aerial camera translates above landscape or subject.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Fly forward at 15 m altitude, gradually reveal solar installation.

catalog.name: Top-down aerial descent
catalog.definition: Camera points down while vertically descending.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Descend from 30 m to 8 m while maintaining nadir angle.

catalog.name: FPV dive / swoop
catalog.definition: Fast dynamic aerial or virtual flight with banking and rapid altitude change.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Swoop down between towers, bank 20 degrees, stabilize at destination.

catalog.name: Roll / Dutch roll
catalog.definition: Rotate camera around lens optical axis.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Roll camera clockwise 10 degrees over 3 seconds; position fixed.

catalog.name: Boom / diagonal rise
catalog.definition: Move camera on combined vertical and lateral path.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Boom up and right 1 m each, maintaining focus on the main actuator.

catalog.name: Parallax slide
catalog.definition: Move laterally with foreground and background at different depths.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Slide 1 m left with foreground piston at 0.5 m and robot behind at 4 m.

catalog.name: Push-through
catalog.definition: Camera passes through a real opening, doorway, or structural gap.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Travel through open hangar hatch into the central engineering bay.

catalog.name: Rack-and-track move
catalog.definition: Camera moves while shifting focus between depth planes.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Dolly 1 m right and rack focus from forearm linkage to background sensors.

catalog.name: Snap zoom
catalog.definition: Very fast focal-length change, typically punchy or comedic.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Snap zoom from medium to close-up in under 0.3 seconds.

catalog.name: Locked-on counter-move
catalog.definition: Camera moves to compensate for subject so its screen position stays stable.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Track robot moving left while holding its eye module near frame center.

catalog.name: Virtual impossible camera
catalog.definition: CG/AI-specific movement not feasible with physical rigs.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Flow from extreme macro of gear teeth into a wide factory view without a hard cut.
catalog.usage: creative virtual scenes; high continuity risk

catalog.name: Eye level
catalog.definition: Lens sits near subject eye height or corresponding interaction height.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Camera at robot sensor height, optical axis horizontal.

catalog.name: Low angle
catalog.definition: Lens below subject and angled upward, increasing apparent dominance.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Set camera at 0.5 m, tilt up 15 degrees toward chassis.

catalog.name: High angle
catalog.definition: Lens above subject and angled downward.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Camera 2.5 m above floor, pitch down 25 degrees.

catalog.name: Birds-eye view
catalog.definition: Elevated camera looks strongly downward, not necessarily vertical.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Camera at 12 m, tilt down 70 degrees.

catalog.name: Nadir / true top-down
catalog.definition: Optical axis points vertically toward the ground.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Camera directly above subject, pitch down 90 degrees.

catalog.name: Worms-eye view
catalog.definition: Extremely low camera pointed steeply upward.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Camera 10 cm above ground, tilt up 60 degrees.

catalog.name: Dutch / canted angle
catalog.definition: Horizon intentionally tilted by camera roll.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Hold 8-degree clockwise Dutch angle.

catalog.name: Front-on / head-on
catalog.definition: Camera faces primary front axis of subject.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Align camera directly with rover nose at wheel height.

catalog.name: Profile / side-on
catalog.definition: Camera faces subject at approximately 90 degrees from its forward axis.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Shoot left-side profile; keep both front and rear wheels visible.

catalog.name: Three-quarter front
catalog.definition: Camera located roughly 30-60 degrees off front axis.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Front-left 45-degree view, 1.2 m height.

catalog.name: Three-quarter rear
catalog.definition: Camera roughly 30-60 degrees off rear axis.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Rear-right 45-degree angle, show propulsion and service hatch.

catalog.name: Over-the-shoulder (OTS)
catalog.definition: Frame past foreground shoulder/edge toward another subject or target.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Frame over technician shoulder toward robotic control screen.

catalog.name: Point of view (POV)
catalog.definition: Camera adopts viewpoint of a character, robot or sensor.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: POV from rover forward navigation camera at 1 m.

catalog.name: Reverse angle
catalog.definition: Shot from roughly opposite facing direction to prior camera.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Cut to 180-degree reverse of the inspection conversation.

catalog.name: Ground-level / tire-level
catalog.definition: Lens placed close to ground or moving equipment contact plane.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Place lens 20 cm high, camera aimed along tire tread.

catalog.name: Axial / centered symmetry
catalog.definition: Camera centered on an object symmetry axis.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Place camera at central chassis midline; straight verticals.

catalog.name: Oblique / diagonal
catalog.definition: View crosses subject rather than matching principal axes.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Frame diagonal workshop lines behind the robot.

catalog.name: Underslung / undercarriage
catalog.definition: Camera located beneath or beside the subject looking up at underside.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Look under chassis from ground to reveal suspension and battery shield.

catalog.name: Isometric-like
catalog.definition: Three visible sides with restrained perspective distortion; not true orthographic unless specified.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Elevated 35-degree three-quarter viewpoint, long lens for compressed perspective.

catalog.name: Aerial oblique
catalog.definition: Aerial camera aimed diagonally toward environment.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Drone 25 m high, camera pitched down 40 degrees.

catalog.name: Extreme wide shot (EWS) / extreme long shot
catalog.definition: Subject small relative to setting; environment carries meaning.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Show 50 m lunar installation with rover occupying under 10% frame width.

catalog.name: Wide shot (WS) / long shot
catalog.definition: Full subject and meaningful surrounding space visible.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Full rover from tire to sensor mast, with terrain on all sides.

catalog.name: Full shot
catalog.definition: Entire subject visible with relatively little surplus environment.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Fit all four wheels and complete antenna within safe margins.

catalog.name: Medium wide shot (MWS)
catalog.definition: Most of subject plus some context; between wide and medium.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Frame robot from feet to upper torso with workshop context.

catalog.name: Medium shot (MS)
catalog.definition: A moderate portion of subject is prominent.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Frame robotic upper body and both manipulator arms.

catalog.name: Medium close-up (MCU)
catalog.definition: Head/shoulder analog or upper assembly fills frame.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Frame sensor head and shoulder actuator together.

catalog.name: Close-up (CU)
catalog.definition: Single meaningful subject part dominates frame.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Fill frame with wheel hub and tread blocks.

catalog.name: Extreme close-up (ECU)
catalog.definition: Tiny component or feature dominates screen.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Macro on engraved bolt head and machining marks.

catalog.name: Insert shot
catalog.definition: Dedicated shot of an object/detail important to story.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Insert: diagnostic light changes from amber to cyan.

catalog.name: Cutaway
catalog.definition: Temporarily shifts from main action to associated detail or observer.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Cut away to servo gear turning while rover stops.

catalog.name: Two-shot
catalog.definition: Two primary subjects in one frame.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Frame human engineer alongside service android.

catalog.name: Group / ensemble
catalog.definition: Three or more primary subjects arranged together.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Show three autonomous robots cooperating around solar array.

catalog.name: Establishing shot
catalog.definition: Introduces setting, geography and subject relationships.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Wide facility exterior followed by robot bay interior.

catalog.name: Master shot
catalog.definition: Continuous broad coverage of scene main action.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Hold full robot assembly process in one wide shot.

catalog.name: Clean single
catalog.definition: One unobstructed isolated subject in frame.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Single robot in frame, no foreground operator.

catalog.name: Negative space
catalog.definition: Intentional empty area around subject.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Place rover in left third with open sky at right.

catalog.name: Centered composition
catalog.definition: Subject placed near central axis.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Center the robot with equal side clearance.

catalog.name: Rule-of-thirds
catalog.definition: Subject aligned near one-third intersections or verticals.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Place sensor head on upper-right thirds intersection.

catalog.name: Leading lines
catalog.definition: Lines in environment direct eye toward subject.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Use rail tracks converging toward fabrication robot.

catalog.name: Foreground framing
catalog.definition: Scene includes foreground objects as a framing device.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Frame rover between two out-of-focus structural beams.

catalog.name: Silhouette
catalog.definition: Subject shape read predominantly against brighter background.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Backlight walking mech at hangar doorway.

catalog.name: Overhead flat lay
catalog.definition: Organize small parts on a plane from a true overhead view.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Arrange disassembled servo parts in precise top-down layout.

catalog.name: Wide-angle lens
catalog.definition: Short focal lengths widen field of view and exaggerate near/far size relationships.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Use 24 mm equivalent; avoid subject-edge warping.

catalog.name: Normal lens
catalog.definition: Approximately natural-looking perspective at common framing distances.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Use 50 mm full-frame equivalent for practical industrial realism.

catalog.name: Telephoto lens
catalog.definition: Long focal lengths narrow view and compress apparent depth across a fixed subject framing.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Use 100 mm equivalent from a distant position, shallow background.

catalog.name: Macro lens
catalog.definition: Close focusing for small details; depth of field often very narrow.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: 90 mm macro, shallow depth of field on machined thread.

catalog.name: Deep focus
catalog.definition: Foreground and background both visually sharp.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Keep wheels, cabin, and rear landscape in sharp focus.

catalog.name: Shallow depth of field
catalog.definition: Narrow distance range appears sharp; near and far elements blur.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Sharp focus on actuator; blurred distant service bay.

catalog.name: Rack focus / focus pull
catalog.definition: Shift focus from one depth plane to another during a single shot.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Rack focus foreground tread to background lidar module in 2 seconds.

catalog.name: Follow focus
catalog.definition: Adjust focus continually to maintain moving subject sharpness.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Maintain sensor eye sharp as robot moves toward lens.

catalog.name: Anamorphic aesthetic
catalog.definition: Wide frame, oval bokeh and characteristic horizontal flare (can be subtle).
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Subtle 2x anamorphic look; avoid exaggerated sci-fi flares.

catalog.name: Slow motion
catalog.definition: Play footage slower than action occurs, usually by high capture frame rate.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: 50% slow-motion playback of hydraulic compression.

catalog.name: Speed ramp
catalog.definition: Change playback speed within one shot.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Ease from 100% to 35% speed at moment of impact, then back.

catalog.name: Timelapse
catalog.definition: Compress long activity into a short shot.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Time-lapse robotic construction over a full daylight cycle.

catalog.name: Motion blur
catalog.definition: Exposure-related blur on moving subjects or camera; should remain physically coherent.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Natural 180-degree shutter motion blur at 24 fps.

catalog.name: Panoramic stitch
catalog.definition: Combine views for a wider scene, generally in post-production.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Stitch a wide static facility panorama; preserve straight structures.

catalog.name: Match cut
catalog.definition: Edit transition matching composition, shape, movement, or idea between two shots.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Match circular tire hub to rotating orbital ring in next shot.

catalog.name: J-cut / L-cut
catalog.definition: Audio begins before or continues after a picture cut, respectively.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Bring motor sound in two seconds before revealing source.

catalog.name: Whip-pan transition
catalog.definition: Join shots during fast blurred pan to mask cut.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: Match leftward blur direction on both sides of the cut.

catalog.name: Push-in transition
catalog.definition: Visual cut between shots aligned on increasing scale or forward motion.
catalog.agent_instruction_example: End the hallway push-in on a component, start close-up from same angle.
